## Package limestest

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/limestest"`

Package limestest holds a consumer's mapping of limes's errors to the error contract it was written against (docs/compatibility.md). A code answered with another status or category is a break, yet it compiles: a consumer mapping categories onto its transport goes on building, and answers otherwise. Pin what the consumer's own transport answers each code with, and a limes that makes it answer otherwise fails the consumer's test instead of its traffic:

	func TestErrorContract(t *testing.T) {
		limestest.CheckMapping(t, map[limes.Code]connect.Code{
			"revoked": connect.CodeUnauthenticated,
			// …
		}, func(c limes.Code) connect.Code {
			p, _ := limes.ProblemOfCode(c)
			return connectCode(p)
		}, limestest.WithoutExchange())
	}

CheckCodes is CheckMapping of every code to its HTTP status and category, for a consumer that answers in HTTP's terms.

<a id="limestest.CheckCategories"></a>

### limestest.CheckCategories

```go
func CheckCategories(t testing.TB, mapped func(limes.Category) bool)
```

CheckCategories fails t for every category of limes.Categories() that mapped reports it does not map: one added after the consumer's mapping was written, which that mapping answers by its default until it maps it (docs/errors.md, "Categories").

<sub>[limestest/limestest.go](../../limestest/limestest.go)</sub>
<a id="limestest.CheckMapping"></a>

### limestest.CheckMapping

```go
func CheckMapping[T comparable](t testing.TB, pinned map[limes.Code]T, answer func(limes.Code) T, opts ...Option)
```

CheckMapping fails t for every way the consumer's answer to limes's codes — every one, but those opts leave out — differs from pinned, its record of the answers its mapping was written to give: a code answer maps otherwise than pinned, a code not pinned — unless AcceptNewByCategory passes it — and a code pinned that is not checked: which limes no longer answers, or opts left out. Each failure of a code checked names the entry to pin, so the first failing run writes the table; failures come in the order of their codes' names, which no release changes: those of the codes checked first, then those of the codes pinned and not checked.

<sub>[limestest/limestest.go](../../limestest/limestest.go)</sub>
<a id="limestest.Option"></a>

### limestest.Option

```go
type Option func(*checked)
```

Option loosens a check, each in one way a consumer asks for by name. They are of two kinds, which do different things:

  - Without… choose the codes a check walks: each leaves out the codes of one component the consumer does not run. They narrow what is checked, and check the rest as strictly.
  - Accept… loosen how a code walked and not pinned is judged: AcceptNewByCategory passes such a code that the consumer answers as its category. It checks every code, and fails on fewer.

None leaves out a code alone. With none, a check walks every code, and a code limes adds fails it until it is pinned: that default is the strictest there is, and no option will change it.

<sub>[limestest/limestest.go](../../limestest/limestest.go)</sub>
<a id="limestest.AcceptNewByCategory"></a>

#### limestest.AcceptNewByCategory

```go
func AcceptNewByCategory() Option
```

AcceptNewByCategory passes a code that is not pinned when the consumer answers it as it answers every code pinned in its category, and there is one: a code limes adds to a category the consumer maps whole then passes, while a pinned code moved to another category still fails, as does a code in a category with none pinned, or one whose pinned codes are answered apart.

A code it passes so fails nothing, and the check names it only in its log, in one line, which go test shows with -v alone: a green run without it says nothing of the table falling behind. Run the check with -v, or now and then without this option, to pin the codes it took.

<sub>[limestest/limestest.go](../../limestest/limestest.go)</sub>

```go

```

WithoutExchange leaves the exchange's codes out of a check, for a consumer that runs no exchange (module exchange): it never meets them, and pins none.


<a id="storetest"></a><a id="package-storetest"></a>

## Package storetest

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/storetest"`

Package storetest checks a limes.Store — and, when it is one, a limes.BiscuitRevocationStore — against the module's contract, the way testing/fstest checks an fs.FS. Run it from the store's own tests:

	func TestStoreContract(t *testing.T) {
		storetest.Run(t, func(t *testing.T) storetest.Env { … })
	}

The checks cover what every caller relies on: a record reads back as it was written and is no caller's to change, a duplicate or unknown id is refused with the module's sentinel, Insert refuses a lineage it could not keep whole — a child past MaxDelegationDepth among it — and a tenant it cannot mint for, revocation reaches every descendant down to MaxDelegationDepth and outlasts time passing, purging drops a record with its revocation entries once it has been expired long enough — in batches, never before its children and never inside a verifier's leeway — listing pages in a fixed order and keeps tenants apart, and a Biscuit copy revokes on its own. When the store implements limes.TenantRecordEraser, erasing a tenant keeps what a verifier still needs; when Env.ScopesTenants is set, a call under another tenant's scope is refused with limes.ErrScopeMismatch, and when Env.ReadOnlyCtx is set, every write under a read-only scope is. When Env.Census is set, a census counts each record under one disposition — revoked, through an ancestor too, over expired over active — by tenant and by principal type, a page at a time, and counts no Biscuit copy. When Env.Lister is set, a listing of a tenant's records pages in both orders with no record skipped or repeated, filters by principal type, subject, subject prefix and disposition, gives each record the disposition the census counts it under, and shows no other tenant's, while one of every tenant's gives them all in one id order; when the lister is a limes.RecordListingReader too, it reads each record as the listing gives it. When Env.BulkRevoker is set, each selector revokes exactly its capabilities, a batch at a time, in one tenant or, by client, session or subject issuer, in every tenant under Env.AllTenantsCtx alone, and a record's session and subject issuer read back, a child's its parent's; with Env.Census and Env.Lister too, a count and a listing by the same selectors name what it revokes. When Env.Exchanges is set, the first claim of a subject token wins, racing ones included, and Purge keeps the claim past its capability while the token can still be presented. A check that does not finish within Env.CheckTimeout stops the test binary with every goroutine's stack, naming the check.

<sub>[storetest/storetest.go](../../storetest/storetest.go)</sub>
<a id="storetest.Env"></a>

### storetest.Env

```go
type Env struct {
	// Ctx is the context every call for Tenant runs under — scoped to it, if
	// the store needs that. A write for a tenant from NewTenant runs under
	// TenantCtx, when the Env sets it.
	Ctx context.Context
	// Store is the store under test, with nothing on record.
	Store limes.Store
	// Tenant is a tenant the store can record capabilities for.
	Tenant uuid.UUID
	// NewTenant creates another tenant the store can record capabilities
	// for, for the checks that need more than one. Optional: without it, a
	// random id, which a store that refers to its tenants refuses.
	NewTenant func() (uuid.UUID, error)
	// TenantCtx is the context a write for tenant — one NewTenant created —
	// runs under, when the store scopes each tenant's rows; Tenant's own
	// calls run under Ctx. Optional: without it, Ctx.
	TenantCtx func(tenant uuid.UUID) context.Context
	// ScopesTenants reports that the store keeps each tenant's rows apart
	// by the call's context, TenantCtx giving each tenant's: a call whose
	// request names one tenant, made under another tenant's context, is
	// refused with limes.ErrScopeMismatch and changes nothing. Optional:
	// without it, the checks of that are skipped.
	ScopesTenants bool
	// ReadOnlyCtx is a context scoped to reading every tenant's rows and
	// writing none, as the store's consumer scopes it — by the store's own
	// context or by a scope of the consumer's: Tenant's records read under
	// it, and every call that writes is refused with
	// limes.ErrScopeMismatch and changes nothing. Optional: without it, the
	// checks of that are skipped.
	ReadOnlyCtx context.Context
	// Now reads the store's clock, which stands still while a check runs
	// but for Advance. Optional: without it, the checks at an expiry's exact
	// instant are skipped, and the checks read the wall clock.
	Now func() time.Time
	// Advance moves the store's clock forward by d. Optional: without it,
	// the checks of what time passing must leave alone are skipped.
	Advance func(d time.Duration)
	// DeleteTenant moves a tenant NewTenant created to the trash, for a
	// store that knows its tenants: it then refuses an id it never created
	// as ErrUnknownTenant and one in the trash as ErrTenantDeleted.
	// Optional: without it, those checks are skipped.
	DeleteTenant func(tenant uuid.UUID) error
	// CheckTimeout bounds one check, setup aside: past it the suite panics
	// with every goroutine's stack, naming the check, rather than leave a
	// deadlocked store to go test's -timeout. Optional: without it,
	// DefaultCheckTimeout.
	CheckTimeout time.Duration
	// Census counts the store's records. Optional: without it, or without
	// Now, the checks of limes.RecordCensus are skipped. A count across
	// every tenant runs under ReadOnlyCtx when the Env sets it, else Ctx.
	Census limes.RecordCensus
	// Lister lists the store's records. Optional: without it, or without
	// Now, the checks of limes.RecordLister are skipped; without Census
	// too, so are those that hold a listing to the census's counts.
	Lister limes.RecordLister
	// Exchanges records the capability exchanging a subject token issued,
	// over the same records as Store. Optional: without it, the checks of
	// limes.ExchangeStore are skipped.
	Exchanges limes.ExchangeStore
	// BulkRevoker revokes by subject, client, session, on-behalf-of, agent
	// run or subject issuer over the same records as Store, which then
	// records each capability's session and subject issuer. Optional:
	// without it, the checks of limes.BulkRevoker and of sessions and
	// subject issuers on record are skipped.
	BulkRevoker limes.BulkRevoker
	// AllTenantsCtx is a context scoped to writing every tenant's rows, as
	// housekeeping is (pgstore.WithAllTenants), for a revocation across
	// tenants. Optional: without it, Ctx, but for a store that scopes
	// tenants, whose checks of that are then skipped.
	AllTenantsCtx context.Context
}
```

Env is one store under test, fresh for each check. Its fields mirror metertest.Env, so one setup can serve both suites.

<a id="metertest"></a><a id="package-metertest"></a>

## Package metertest

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/metertest"`

Package metertest checks a meter.UsageStore against the module's contract — its Meter, tenant budgets and housekeeping — the way testing/fstest checks an fs.FS. A UsageStore is the consumer's to write, and most of its contract lives in request fields: a store that ignores ExternalRef or Overrun still compiles, and then charges a repeated cost twice. Run it from the store's own tests:

	func TestMeterContract(t *testing.T) {
		metertest.Run(t, func(t *testing.T) metertest.Env { … })
	}

A store that counts requests and spends nothing, a meter.RequestCounter, runs RunCounter instead: the checks of Bump alone, which Run runs too.

The checks cover what a charge does at its ceilings and when it arrives again: rejection that moves nothing — by a Biscuit copy's, the capability's, an ancestor's or the tenant's ceiling, by a failed onCharged or onRefunded, under concurrent charges, siblings' and grandchildren's among them — idempotency on ExternalRef and on a settled reservation, also once the capability is gone (Env.DeleteCapability), on a ReservationID and on a RefundID, which goes with its charge; ChargeByRef, OverrunPolicyRecord past every ceiling, refunds, holds, their listing and their expiry, request counts, copy counters and CopyUsage, units, counters that never pass MaxNanos, a capability not on record and PurgeOrphans (Env.DeleteCapability), DeleteUsage, the tenant aggregate, its version guard and its listing, and the validation of the request. Where the store or the Env enables them, they cover leases (meter.Leaser), EraseTenantUsage, ReleaseMatching, ListTenantReservations, limes.ErrScopeMismatch under another tenant's scope and for every write under a read-only one, a LedgerReader's sums, their order, paging, UTC buckets, period edges, late refunds and overflow, and, when the Ledger is a meter.LedgerHousekeeping, PurgeCharges to its retention. They need a real ledger, not a fake.

Concurrent calls that each promise to move one thing once — refunds of one charge, settles and releases of one hold, top-ups of one lease, charges racing EraseTenantUsage, writes of a tenant ceiling at one version — are held to moving it once.

Several checks call the store from many goroutines at once. Give the Env a connection pool of one or two connections: a call that takes a second connection while it holds its transaction then deadlocks here, not under a production load. A check that does not finish within Env.CheckTimeout stops the test binary with every goroutine's stack, naming the check.

<a id="metertest.RunCounter"></a>

### metertest.RunCounter

```go
func RunCounter(t *testing.T, setup func(t *testing.T) CounterEnv)
```

RunCounter runs the checks of meter.RequestCounter as subtests, each on a fresh CounterEnv from setup. They read nothing but Bump's receipts and refusals, so a store that counts requests and nothing else passes them: a capability's own ceiling, an ancestor's from its record bounding its whole subtree, a chain at the deepest delegation, a Biscuit copy's ceiling, a refusal that counts nothing, concurrent bumps at a ceiling, siblings' at their root's among them, the zero ceiling and subject, a capability not on record, and, where the CounterEnv enables them, an ancestor removed, another tenant's scope and a read-only one.

Run runs these checks too, on its Env's store.

<a id="metertest.CapabilitySpec"></a>

### metertest.CapabilitySpec

```go
type CapabilitySpec struct {
	// Parent is the capability it was delegated from; uuid.Nil() for a root.
	Parent uuid.UUID
	// Tenant is the tenant it is issued in, one NewTenant created; uuid.Nil()
	// for Env.Tenant.
	Tenant uuid.UUID
	// Requests and Budget are its caveats' ceilings; Budget names the unit
	// the capability counts in.
	Requests limes.RequestCeiling
	Budget   limes.BudgetCeiling
	// Copies is its quota of Biscuit copies; nil is Unlimited. CopyQuota
	// reads it as the record should hold it.
	Copies *limes.CopyQuota
	// ClientID is the client it is granted to, which the record holds as
	// Capability.ClientID; empty for none.
	ClientID string
	// SubjectIssuer is the issuer of the subject token it was exchanged for,
	// which the record holds as limes.InsertRequest.SubjectIssuer; empty for
	// none. A child takes its parent's.
	SubjectIssuer string
}
```

CapabilitySpec is a capability Env.NewCapability records: its parent and the ceilings of its caveats.

<a id="metertest.CounterEnv"></a>

### metertest.CounterEnv

```go
type CounterEnv struct {
	// Ctx is the context every call for Tenant runs under.
	Ctx context.Context
	// Counter is the store under test, with no request counted.
	Counter meter.RequestCounter
	// Tenant is a tenant the store can count for.
	Tenant uuid.UUID
	// NewCapability records a capability of Tenant as spec describes it, so
	// the counter finds its lineage and its ceilings, and returns its id.
	// Its Budget is the unlimited one in the suite's unit.
	NewCapability func(spec CapabilitySpec) (uuid.UUID, error)
	// CheckTimeout bounds one check. Optional: without it,
	// DefaultCheckTimeout.
	CheckTimeout time.Duration
	// DeleteCapability removes a capability's record, as Store.Purge does.
	// Optional: without it, the checks of a capability or an ancestor no
	// longer on record are skipped.
	DeleteCapability func(id uuid.UUID) error
	// NewTenant creates another tenant. Optional: without it, a random id.
	NewTenant func() (uuid.UUID, error)
	// TenantCtx is the context a call for tenant runs under. Optional:
	// without it, Ctx.
	TenantCtx func(tenant uuid.UUID) context.Context
	// ScopesTenants reports that a Bump made under another tenant's context
	// is refused with limes.ErrScopeMismatch and counts nothing. Optional:
	// without it, that check is skipped.
	ScopesTenants bool
	// ReadOnlyCtx is a context scoped to reading, writing nothing, under
	// which a Bump is refused with limes.ErrScopeMismatch. Optional: without
	// it, that check is skipped.
	ReadOnlyCtx context.Context
}
```

CounterEnv is one meter.RequestCounter under test, fresh for each check. Its fields mean what Env's of the same name do.

<a id="metertest.Env"></a>

### metertest.Env

```go
type Env struct {
	// Ctx is the context every call for Tenant runs under — scoped to it, if
	// the store needs that. A write for a tenant from NewTenant runs under
	// TenantCtx, and ListTenantBudgets under ListCtx, when the Env sets them.
	Ctx context.Context
	// Usage is the store under test, with no usage recorded.
	Usage meter.UsageStore
	// Tenant is a tenant the store can charge, with no ceiling yet.
	Tenant uuid.UUID
	// NewCapability records a capability of Tenant as spec describes it, so
	// the Meter finds its lineage and its ceilings, and returns its id — or
	// the error the store's Insert returned, which the checks match by its
	// sentinel.
	NewCapability func(spec CapabilitySpec) (uuid.UUID, error)
	// CheckTimeout bounds one check, setup aside: past it the suite panics
	// with every goroutine's stack, naming the check, rather than leave a
	// deadlocked store to go test's -timeout. Optional: without it,
	// DefaultCheckTimeout.
	CheckTimeout time.Duration
	// Advance moves the store's clock forward by d. Optional: without it,
	// the checks that need time to pass are skipped or cut short — a hold's
	// and a lease's expiry and ReleaseExpired, its batches, a hold dating the
	// tenant budget, the accounting period's start, the ledger's buckets,
	// period edges and late refunds, and PurgeCharges.
	Advance func(d time.Duration)
	// DeleteCapability removes a capability's record, as Store.Purge does
	// once it has expired. Optional: without it, the checks of what follows
	// a record's removal are skipped or cut short — PurgeOrphans, a replay
	// once the capability is gone, a settle under a removed ancestor, a
	// chain's depth once its top is removed, a capability not on record,
	// and a copy's counters going with their capability.
	//
	// Some checks remove an ancestor whose children stay on record, which
	// Purge never does: a store whose records refer to their parent (a
	// foreign key) unhooks the children first, leaving each a root, as its
	// lineage reads once the ancestor is gone. pgstore's own test does it
	// in one statement: UPDATE the children's parent to none, then DELETE.
	DeleteCapability func(id uuid.UUID) error
	// NewTenant creates another tenant the store can charge, for the checks
	// that need more than one. Optional: without it, a random id, which a
	// store that refers to its tenants refuses.
	NewTenant func() (uuid.UUID, error)
	// TenantCtx is the context a write for tenant — one NewTenant created —
	// runs under, when the store scopes each tenant's rows; Tenant's own
	// calls run under Ctx. Optional: without it, Ctx.
	TenantCtx func(tenant uuid.UUID) context.Context
	// ListCtx is the context ListTenantBudgets runs under: a read across
	// tenants. Optional: without it, Ctx.
	ListCtx context.Context
	// Ledger reads the store's charges ledger. Optional: without it, the
	// checks of meter.LedgerReader are skipped.
	Ledger meter.LedgerReader
	// Now reads the store's clock, which stands still while a check runs
	// but for Advance. Optional: without it, the checks of the ledger's
	// buckets, period edges and late refunds, of PurgeCharges, of a hold
	// ending with its capability and of a hold dating the tenant budget are
	// skipped.
	Now func() time.Time
	// ExpiryNow and AdvanceExpiry read and move the clock the store
	// measures holds' and leases' expiry by, where that is not the clock Now
	// and Advance read and move: pgstore's, built with no clock of its own,
	// measures them by the database's. The checks of expiry — a hold's and a
	// lease's, ReleaseExpired, a hold ending with its capability — use them;
	// ExpiryNow may run on while a check runs. Optional: without them, Now
	// and Advance. An Env that sets them and leaves Now and Advance unset
	// runs the checks of expiry on that clock and skips those that need the
	// store's own clock to move.
	ExpiryNow     func() time.Time
	AdvanceExpiry func(d time.Duration)
	// ScopesTenants reports that the store keeps each tenant's rows apart
	// by the call's context, TenantCtx giving each tenant's: a call whose
	// request names one tenant, made under another tenant's context, is
	// refused with limes.ErrScopeMismatch and changes nothing. Optional:
	// without it, the checks of that are skipped.
	ScopesTenants bool
	// MaxCopiesPerCapability is the quota of Biscuit copies per capability
	// the store under test was built with (meter.Meter, "Copies of a
	// Biscuit"). Optional: without it, the check of the quota is skipped. Set
	// it above any check's own copies — 16 is room enough.
	MaxCopiesPerCapability int
	// ReadOnlyCtx is a context scoped to reading every tenant's rows and
	// writing none, as the store's consumer scopes it — by the store's own
	// context or by a scope of the consumer's: Tenant's usage reads under
	// it, and every call that writes is refused with
	// limes.ErrScopeMismatch, runs no onCharged and changes nothing.
	// Optional: without it, the checks of that are skipped.
	ReadOnlyCtx context.Context
	// Revoke revokes the record of a capability NewCapability recorded, as
	// Store.Revoke does. Optional: without it, or when Usage is no
	// meter.MatchingReleaser, the checks of ReleaseMatching are skipped.
	Revoke func(id uuid.UUID) error
	// AllTenantsCtx is a context scoped to writing every tenant's rows, as
	// housekeeping is (pgstore.WithAllTenants), for a release across
	// tenants. Optional: without it, Ctx, but for a store that scopes
	// tenants, whose checks of that are then skipped.
	AllTenantsCtx context.Context
	// HoldTenantAlone takes what the store's period reset and its erase of
	// a tenant's usage take on tenant alone — pgstore's erase lock, a
	// store's own mutex — and holds it until release is called. Optional:
	// without it, the check that every call ending a hold, a lease or a
	// charge waits for a tenant held alone is skipped.
	HoldTenantAlone func(tenant uuid.UUID) (release func())
}
```

Env is one store under test, fresh for each check.

<a id="dpoptest"></a><a id="package-dpoptest"></a>

## Package dpoptest

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/dpop/dpoptest"`

Package dpoptest checks a dpop.ReplayCache and a dpop.Nonces against the package's contract, the way storetest checks a limes.Store. Run them from the implementation's own tests:

	func TestReplayCacheContract(t *testing.T) {
		dpoptest.RunReplayCache(t, func(t *testing.T) dpoptest.ReplayEnv { … })
	}

The checks cover what the verifier relies on: a proof id is new once and a replay ever after, while it can still be accepted; ids of different keys never collide; a holder's share counts its proofs whatever key signed them, and one past it is refused with dpop.ErrReplayQuota rather than as a replay, until its ids expire; concurrent proofs carrying one id let exactly one through; a nonce issued is valid, and one never issued or expired is not.

<a id="dpoptest.DefaultCheckTimeout"></a>

### dpoptest.DefaultCheckTimeout

```go
const DefaultCheckTimeout = watchdog.DefaultLimit
```

DefaultCheckTimeout bounds a check whose ReplayEnv or NoncesEnv sets no CheckTimeout.

<sub>[dpop/dpoptest/dpoptest.go](../../dpop/dpoptest/dpoptest.go)</sub>

### dpoptest.RunNonces

```go
func RunNonces(t *testing.T, setup func(t *testing.T) NoncesEnv)
```

<sub>[dpop/dpoptest/dpoptest.go](../../dpop/dpoptest/dpoptest.go)</sub>
<a id="dpoptest.RunReplayCache"></a>

### dpoptest.RunReplayCache

```go
func RunReplayCache(t *testing.T, setup func(t *testing.T) ReplayEnv)
```

RunReplayCache runs every replay cache check as a subtest, each on a fresh ReplayEnv from setup.

<sub>[dpop/dpoptest/dpoptest.go](../../dpop/dpoptest/dpoptest.go)</sub>
<a id="dpoptest.NoncesEnv"></a>

### dpoptest.NoncesEnv

```go
type NoncesEnv struct {
	// Ctx is the context every call runs under.
	Ctx context.Context
	// Nonces is the nonce source under test.
	Nonces dpop.Nonces
	// Lifetime is how long a nonce is valid. Optional, with Advance:
	// without both, the check of expiry is skipped.
	Lifetime time.Duration
	// Advance moves the source's clock forward by d.
	Advance func(d time.Duration)
	// CheckTimeout bounds one check, setup aside: past it the suite panics
	// with every goroutine's stack, naming the check, rather than leave a
	// deadlocked source to go test's -timeout. Optional: without it,
	// DefaultCheckTimeout.
	CheckTimeout time.Duration
}
```

NoncesEnv is one nonce source under test, fresh for each check.

<sub>[dpop/dpoptest/dpoptest.go](../../dpop/dpoptest/dpoptest.go)</sub>
<a id="dpoptest.ReplayEnv"></a>

### dpoptest.ReplayEnv

```go
type ReplayEnv struct {
	// Ctx is the context every call runs under.
	Ctx context.Context
	// Cache is the cache under test, with no id recorded.
	Cache dpop.ReplayCache
	// Now reads the cache's clock. Optional: without it, time.Now.
	Now func() time.Time
	// Advance moves the cache's clock forward by d. Optional, with Now:
	// without both, the checks that an id is remembered until it expires
	// and that a holder's share frees once its ids expire are skipped.
	Advance func(d time.Duration)
	// EntriesPerHolder is how many live ids the cache holds for one holder
	// before it refuses the next with dpop.ErrReplayQuota. Optional: without
	// it, the checks of that share are skipped.
	EntriesPerHolder int
	// CheckTimeout bounds one check, setup aside: past it the suite panics
	// with every goroutine's stack, naming the check, rather than leave a
	// deadlocked cache to go test's -timeout. Optional: without it,
	// DefaultCheckTimeout.
	CheckTimeout time.Duration
}
```

ReplayEnv is one replay cache under test, fresh and empty for each check.

<sub>[dpop/dpoptest/dpoptest.go](../../dpop/dpoptest/dpoptest.go)</sub>

<a id="jwkstest"></a><a id="package-jwkstest"></a>

## Package jwkstest

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/jwks/jwkstest"`

Package jwkstest checks a limes.KeyResolver against the module's contract, the way storetest checks a limes.Store. Run it from the resolver's own tests:

	func TestKeyResolverContract(t *testing.T) {
		jwkstest.Run(t, func(t *testing.T) jwkstest.Env { … })
	}

The checks cover what the verifier relies on: a kid the resolver knows gives its key, one it does not is jwks.ErrUnknownKID — the token's fault, not the resolver's — and concurrent lookups agree.

<a id="jwkstest.DefaultCheckTimeout"></a>

### jwkstest.DefaultCheckTimeout

```go
const DefaultCheckTimeout = watchdog.DefaultLimit
```

DefaultCheckTimeout bounds a check whose Env sets no CheckTimeout.

<sub>[jwks/jwkstest/jwkstest.go](../../jwks/jwkstest/jwkstest.go)</sub>
<a id="jwkstest.Run"></a>

### jwkstest.Run

```go
func Run(t *testing.T, setup func(t *testing.T) Env)
```

Run runs every check as a subtest, each on a fresh Env from setup.

<sub>[jwks/jwkstest/jwkstest.go](../../jwks/jwkstest/jwkstest.go)</sub>
<a id="jwkstest.Env"></a>

### jwkstest.Env

```go
type Env struct {
	// Ctx is the context every call runs under.
	Ctx context.Context
	// Resolver is the resolver under test.
	Resolver limes.KeyResolver
	// KID is a kid the resolver knows.
	KID string
	// Key is the public key the resolver holds under KID.
	Key ed25519.PublicKey
	// CheckTimeout bounds one check, setup aside: past it the suite panics
	// with every goroutine's stack, naming the check, rather than leave a
	// deadlocked resolver to go test's -timeout. Optional: without it,
	// DefaultCheckTimeout.
	CheckTimeout time.Duration
}
```

Env is one resolver under test, fresh for each check, that knows Key under KID and no other kid the checks ask for.

<a id="exchangetest"></a><a id="package-exchangetest"></a>

## Package exchangetest

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/exchange/exchangetest"`

Package exchangetest holds a SubjectVerifier to the contract the Exchanger relies on, for an implementation of your own: one for opaque tokens through introspection, or for a provider whose tokens are not RFC 9068's.

	func TestMyVerifier(t *testing.T) {
		exchangetest.TestSubjectVerifier(t, myVerifier, exchangetest.Tokens{
			Valid:   func(t *testing.T) (string, exchange.Subject) { … },
			Expired: func(t *testing.T) string { … },
			…
		})
	}

<a id="exchangetest.TestOnePerToken"></a>

### exchangetest.TestOnePerToken

```go
func TestOnePerToken(t *testing.T, env OnePerToken)
```

TestOnePerToken holds an Exchanger in one-capability-per-token mode to what that mode promises: a subject token exchanged again, or by exchanges racing, yields one capability and one token; a revoked one is refused, not issued anew; and a token without a jti is refused.

<sub>[exchange/exchangetest/one_per_token.go](../../exchange/exchangetest/one_per_token.go)</sub>
<a id="exchangetest.TestSubjectVerifier"></a>

### exchangetest.TestSubjectVerifier

```go
func TestSubjectVerifier(t *testing.T, v exchange.SubjectVerifier, tokens Tokens)
```

TestSubjectVerifier holds v to what the Exchanger relies on: it reads a valid token as the issuer wrote it, and refuses everything else with exchange.ErrInvalidGrant, which the exchange answers as invalid\_grant; any other error would be answered as the server's failure.

<sub>[exchange/exchangetest/exchangetest.go](../../exchange/exchangetest/exchangetest.go)</sub>
<a id="exchangetest.OnePerToken"></a>

### exchangetest.OnePerToken

```go
type OnePerToken struct {
	Exchanger *exchange.Exchanger
	// Request is an exchange the Exchanger grants, of a subject token no
	// earlier call returned.
	Request func(t *testing.T) exchange.Request
	// NoJTI is an exchange the Exchanger would grant but for its subject
	// token carrying no jti.
	NoJTI func(t *testing.T) exchange.Request
	// Revoke revokes the capability id, as the consumer's operators do.
	Revoke func(t *testing.T, id uuid.UUID)
	// Purge moves the clock past the capabilities' expiry, while the
	// subject tokens Request signs are still live, and purges what expired,
	// as the consumer's housekeeping does: the policy names a TTL shorter
	// than the subject token's.
	Purge func(t *testing.T)
}
```

OnePerToken is an Exchanger set to issue one capability per subject token (exchange.Config.Exchanges), over the consumer's own ExchangeStore, roles and row-level security, and how to drive it. Exchanger and Request are required; a check whose field is nil is skipped, and says so.

<sub>[exchange/exchangetest/one_per_token.go](../../exchange/exchangetest/one_per_token.go)</sub>
<a id="exchangetest.Tokens"></a>

### exchangetest.Tokens

```go
type Tokens struct {
	// Valid is a token the verifier must accept, and the subject it must
	// read from it: issuer, subject, client, audience, expiry and binding.
	Valid func(t *testing.T) (token string, want exchange.Subject)
	// Expired is a token whose lifetime has ended.
	Expired func(t *testing.T) string
	// OtherIssuer is a token from an issuer the verifier does not trust.
	OtherIssuer func(t *testing.T) string
	// Forged is a token signed, or vouched for, by none of the issuer's keys.
	Forged func(t *testing.T) string
	// NoClient is a token that names no client.
	NoClient func(t *testing.T) string
	// Bound is a token bound to a DPoP key, and that key's thumbprint.
	Bound func(t *testing.T) (token, jkt string)
	// Session is a token issued in an identity provider's session, and the
	// session's id, which the verifier reads as Subject.SessionID.
	Session func(t *testing.T) (token, sid string)
}
```

Tokens mints the tokens the suite presents. Valid is required; a refusal left nil is skipped, and says so, since a verifier that cannot be shown one of them may still refuse it.

<sub>[exchange/exchangetest/exchangetest.go](../../exchange/exchangetest/exchangetest.go)</sub>
